b01.text: Bay Museum requests the celestial globe for Navigating at Night, four months from June. Loan committee needs their case specification and light-level plan before approval.
Returning mask from Ash Gallery due next Wednesday. Compare carved edge with the outgoing condition photos before signing receipt.
Globe crate sketch: suspended inner cradle, no pressure on meridian ring. Outside width estimate 82 cm including foam and handles.
Please check the ring before signing. Message forwarded without attachment or sender context.
Paper archive humidity climbs whenever the supply fan stops. Technician wants a week of readings from the independent logger.
Choir altos: pencilled breath after 'water', not before it. Make six copies of the marked score for Monday rehearsal.
Bay sent the globe case drawing with a supported brass base and controlled lights. Committee approved the loan subject to the signed indemnity schedule.
Crate maker measured globe on its base: outside width must be 91 cm, replacing the 82 cm sketch. Larger handles included in the new figure; check the loading-door opening.
Ash mask return condition sheet: old chip beside left eye unchanged, but new scrape on the underside of the stand. Photograph before moving it off the unpacking table.
Courier route sheet has globe outward collection and Ash mask return on the same vehicle. Mask paperwork stays with receiving registrar; globe crate can load only after the return is unloaded.
Archive logger shows peaks at fan stoppages, not when the door opens. Service company bringing a replacement relay on Thursday.

Globe dispatch review with Bay: approve the loan schedule with the revised packed dimensions, and attach the signed case/light conditions to the agreement. Transport team must use a liftgate van because the completed 91 cm crate cannot go through the smaller side door. The host registrar will receive the sealed crate at the loading bay and send the seal photograph before their crew opens it. Committee approval alone is not our dispatch release; release comes after the crate maker confirms the cradle holds the base without touching the meridian ring. Pack a copy of the agreed handling diagram in the outer document pocket so nobody needs to break the seal to find it. Bay's registrar has checked the revised loan schedule and will return the signature page after their facilities team confirms the liftgate arrival slot.
Choir director changed the alto breath: take it before 'water' after all, together with tenors. Mark the correction on all six rehearsal copies.
Ash Gallery agrees the mask stand scrape is new. Registrar will retain the comparison photos and record the accepted repair contribution against this return.
Globe cradle test filmed with dummy load: base stays level through the ramp angle, meridian ring area remains clear. Crate maker signed release sheet.
Bay globe agreement signed by both registrars. Loan dates remain June through September; exhibition credit line now includes the donor family.
New archive relay fitted. Supply fan ran overnight and the paper-room logger stayed inside the set band; keep logging through Monday.
Globe van collected at the agreed bay. Crate seal and liftgate loading photographed; send tracking update to Bay registrar.
Mask return reconciled: receiving signature, scrape photographs and contribution agreement all filed. Move object back to its assigned store shelf.
Monday choir pack ready, six alto scores with the revised breath mark. Keep one crossed-out original so I remember which instruction changed.

b02.text: Loose slip from tote: 'third one too weak; move it' with a smudged arrow.
Embroidered hanging survey: fading strongest along top third, two weak stitches at lower sleeve. Compare against last year's colour target photographs.
Home fence blew over at the corner. Save the undamaged gate; price three replacement panels and two posts.
Hanging tour draft: Bell House in March, Estuary Rooms in April, Hill Centre in May. Each venue wants a full calendar month.
Textile courier coverage: Sal available March only; Mina can do April and May if dates avoid her course. Need someone trained to supervise unrolling.
Survey under raking light shows lower sleeve stitches hold at rest but pull when hanging vertically. Recommend a sloped support board instead of free hanging.
Bell House can build the sloped support. Their conservator asks us to send the exact board angle with the condition report.
Tour revision: Hill Centre cannot control daylight, so remove its May slot. Bell House remains March; Estuary Rooms gets April plus the first week of May.
Mina's course moved to 3 May. She can take the hanging to Estuary in April but cannot supervise its return on 7 May; seek return cover.
'Mina / 7 / angle?' heard over station announcement.
Fence supplier quote is for four panels by mistake. We need three; gate stays. Revised dimensions marked on corner sketch.
Tour renamed from 'Three rooms' to 'Stitched journeys' after dropping Hill Centre. Keep existing Bell House and Estuary agreements under the new project heading.
Textile support trial passed at 20 degrees from vertical. Record the lower sleeve's weak stitches on the courier condition diagram so any change during unpacking can be compared to today's survey.

Stitched journeys return plan: shorten Estuary display to 5 May, when trained courier Arun is free. Amend the venue loan end date and book Arun's return train for the next morning, allowing daylight for the unpacking inspection at our store.
Arun confirmed return travel and received unrolling training sign-off. Mina still handles the April outward move.
Home fence posts now set. Test gate swing after hanging the three panels; neighbour asked us to keep the old latch height.

Condition review limits the embroidered hanging to nine weeks of display at the agreed light level. Annotate the survey report with that cap and reduce Bell House's opening by one week so the revised two-venue tour fits within it; send both venues the amended dates.
Bell House countersigned its shortened dates; Estuary's 5 May close remains. Final Stitched journeys itinerary filed with both agreements.
Keep it flat until Monday. No image attached.
Textile baseline photographs complete with colour target, sleeve detail and 20-degree support view. Use these for the next condition comparison.

b03.text: Fieldmark first-run sketch: ask walkers to name a place, then write their first trail note. Test whether the blank map before that step is making people quit.
Flowers for Asha's wedding: mixed white stems in low bowls, six tables. Florist needs final table count by the 9th.
'Skip fires twice' on a note beside the laptop. No screen or event name recorded.
Fieldmark analytics draft: onboarding_done fires on leaving the last intro card, first_note_saved only after storage confirms success. Need a separate skipped flag.

Onboarding experiment handoff: variant Cedar removes the blank map and opens the first-note editor immediately. Add intro_variant=Cedar to onboarding_done and first_note_saved, then verify both events after a complete first-run walkthrough. The design test still compares the same task: creating a trail note.
Airplane-mode recording: Fieldmark shows 'saved' for a first trail note, but reopening loses it. Reproduces with a fresh install and no network.
Florist sketch uses tall vases, but Asha asked for low bowls so guests can see across tables. Request corrected proposal.
Cedar first-run test with five volunteers: four reached the editor without help; one looked for an account button. Keep the name-place prompt but explain saving before sign-in.
Event trace on fresh install: onboarding_done emitted twice when app returns from background on the last card. Deduplicate by completed onboarding session, not by screen view.
Offline save diagnosis: first launch creates the local store only after a profile fetch. Initialize the store before any network work so the editor can commit without a profile.
Maybe the local one? recording cuts off immediately.
Wedding table count is seven now, not six. Florist can add one matching low bowl; keep the aisle flowers unchanged.

Measurement correction: onboarding_done must fire on explicit Finish or Skip, not any exit from the last card; backgrounding is neither. Keep first_note_saved tied to the storage confirmation as before.
Offline fix test: three notes survive force-close in airplane mode on a fresh install. Reconnection later uploads each once; the local store initializes without a profile.
Cedar copy change: 'Your note stays on this device until you sign in.' Put this under the first-note editor, above the save button; next test should check what users think happens offline.

Release walkthrough for Fieldmark: with the offline-store fix, first_note_saved arrives only after the local commit even without a connection. Test analytics queue replay on reconnect and assert one saved event for the one surviving note; retain the airplane-mode persistence check in the bug's acceptance notes.

Cedar follow-up: all six participants could explain device-only saving after reading the new sentence. Four created a note; two deliberately skipped. Summarize the comprehension finding alongside the task completion counts.
Florist revised order accepted: seven low bowls, unchanged aisle stems. Cousin Dan will return the bowls on Monday; add his name to the rental pickup sheet.
End of debug log only: 'ok 1 queued 1'. Device and action missing.
Analytics validation complete: Finish and Skip each emit one completion with correct skipped value; returning from background emits none. Saved-note event waits for successful local commit.

b04.text: EchoSteps onboarding test: compare microphone permission on launch with asking only when the learner taps Record in lesson one. Prototype label is 'Late mic'.
Pippin needs a walker Tuesday and Thursday while I'm on the early shift. Bea can collect at eight; ask about wet-weather cover.
Spanish onboarding sheet: translator wants screenshots for 'Record', 'Try again' and the sentence explaining microphone access. Text limits differ between buttons and body copy.
First-lesson replay crash recording: finish example audio, tap Replay twice quickly, app closes. Happened after microphone access was denied too.
Experiment report draft: denominator is users who opened lesson one; numerator is users who completed a recording within a day. Break out prompt-on-launch and Late mic cohorts.
Permission prototype interview: learners understood why Record needs the mic, but the launch dialog felt unexplained. Add a one-sentence explanation immediately before the later request.
Pippin walking confirmation: Bea takes Tuesday, Jules Thursday. Spare lead hangs inside the cupboard; both know he shouldn't chase bikes.
Spanish screenshot check: 'Grabar' fits the Record button. The explanatory body sentence wraps to three lines at large text size; allow the panel to grow.
Replay crash stack points to the disposed playback handle. Ignore a second Replay until the first restart has obtained a new handle; cancellation must clear the pending restart.
Rename the 'Late mic' onboarding prototype to 'Ask on Record'. It remains the same request-on-first-record variant; update the review board title and leave the launch-timing control alone.

Report correction: using lesson openers as the denominator drops people put off by the launch permission dialog. Use all newly assigned eligible installs, replacing that draft denominator, and keep completion within a day as numerator.
Pippin soaked the spare lead Tuesday. Put a dry one on the hook before Jules arrives Thursday; Bea's walk itself was fine.
Spanish review of the mic explanation is approved by the translator. Keep 'micrófono' in the body, and use the short verb on the button; export the signed strings sheet.

Ask on Record analysis handoff: freeze the prototype with the explanatory sentence before the permission request, and report outcomes under that final variant name. Rebuild the outcome table from all assigned eligible installs, including those who never reached lesson one; attach the exact screen sequence beside the table so readers know which flow was tested.
Replay fix stress test: ten double-taps after example completion, no crash; leaving the lesson during pending restart cancels cleanly. Repeat once with microphone denied.
Cohort report rebuilt: launch prompt 81/210 completed a recording, Ask on Record 103/214. These are the fixed one-day counts; hold interpretation until checking assignment and missing events.
Ask on Record permission screen at maximum text size: explanation and both actions visible after scrolling. Keep the explicit Not now action in the test build.
Denied-microphone replay check passed: no crash on rapid Replay, and the example audio still works. Close the playback-handle bug.
Spanish onboarding export imported. Screenshots match the signed strings, accents intact, no clipped Record button; translation handoff complete.
'The later one needs checking' — no attachment, subject or quoted message.

b05.text: Pool gate rejected my club card again at dawn. Display says expired even though the desk receipt shows renewal; ask the facility to check the reader clock.
Swim renewal ledger: household Chen, member 083, annual fee received by transfer. Mark active through next August and email the receipt.
Telescope image shakes after focusing. Tripod leg clamps feel solid, but the mount head shifts sideways when touched.
Three swimmers stopped at the gate before 06:00, all admitted later with the same cards. The access schedule may start an hour too late.
Chen 083 correction: transfer was for a three-month membership, not annual. Change expiry to November and issue a corrected renewal receipt; keep the first receipt marked superseded.
Pool controller set to open at 06:00; published member sessions start at 05:00. Facility technician will adjust the schedule tomorrow morning.
083 — loose again?
Mount head bolt is turning with the nut. Hold the underside still while tightening, then retest the telescope at high magnification.
Swimming club renewal reminder drafted for lapsed households. Exclude anyone whose transfer is awaiting reconciliation so we don't ask twice.
Gate schedule corrected. Test one active club card at 05:05 and another after the desk opens; log successful and failed attempts with times.
High-magnification telescope test is steadier after tightening the mount bolt. There is still a small vertical bounce; inspect the tilt hinge next.
Club renewal count: 46 active households, four transfers awaiting names. The treasurer needs reference numbers to match those four payments.
05:05 gate test passed with two cards. Chen's 083 still shows a different expiry in the controller than on the corrected receipt; record it as a separate access-data fault.
Tripod hinge pad has split. Order a replacement pad of the measured thickness; tightening harder would distort the hinge bracket.
Two unnamed swim transfers matched to households using bank references. Their renewal receipts are sent; two payments still need identification.

For Chen 083, correct the club's exported renewal row to November and regenerate the receipt attachment. Then resync that row to the pool gate and test that its displayed expiry matches. Keep both membership and entry logs of the correction.
Pool reader now displays November for 083. Card enters during the early session; photograph the controller status for the closed fault record.
New hinge pad fitted on the telescope mount. Focus test settles immediately; pack the matching spare beside the eyepieces.
Last two swim transfers identified. Annual renewal ledger reconciles to the bank, with Chen recorded as the shorter-term membership.
Early pool entry checks clean for a week. Facility desk can close the gate timing ticket and retain the separate expiry-sync note.

b06.text: Court two surface lifting near the baseline. Contractor estimates a one-day closure next Monday for patching and recoating.
Family badminton day: short taster games, loan racquets, quiet corner for introductions. Advertise Sunday morning with a capped signup list.
Trial club offer draft: four visits for 18, valid six weeks from first use. Track conversions to full membership after the final visit.

At family day registration, issue each interested household the four-visit trial card and enter its first-use date in the membership tracker. Add a ten-minute trial-offer explanation to the event welcome so families understand the expiry.
Balcony door drags on the lower corner when closed. Mark the rub point with chalk and inspect the hinge screws.
Unclaimed hall box: green junior racquet, two water bottles, one shoe bag. Photograph items without showing names on the bottles.
Court contractor revised the closure to three days: coating needs longer to cure. Replace Monday-only notice with Monday through Wednesday and block those bookings.
Green one, four, next week
Family day has 23 signups, including eight children. Split beginner games across both available courts and assign an adult helper to each group.
Trial card ledger: six households started, one has used all four visits. Ask that household whether booking times met their needs before counting a conversion.
Racquet claimant can describe the grip repair under the green tape. Arrange collection of that junior racquet after verifying it matches.
Balcony upper hinge screws were loose. Tightened them; door clears the frame but still needs a pull to latch.
Could move it to Wednesday if she agrees.
Court two after curing: baseline patch flush, but one edge line is uneven. Contractor to repaint that short section before reopening.
Family day welcome sign should say loan racquets available and show where the quiet introduction corner is. Use large type at the entrance.
Four-visit trial feedback: evening slots too scarce for two families. Summarize this constraint in the trial review before proposing a permanent offer.
Junior racquet collected by its owner; shoe bag remains unclaimed. Update the hall lost-property photo so members stop asking about the racquet.
Latch plate moved slightly on the balcony door. It now closes without pulling; test again when the afternoon sun warms the frame.
Photo is too blurred to see whether that's the mark we meant.
Court two reopened after the line repaint and slip check. Remove the closure notice and retain the contractor's three-day curing record.

b07.text: After a day at the home desk, I keep looking down at the laptop. Try the spare monitor on a 12 cm riser and use the laptop closed beside it.
Chair seat is high enough for typing but my heels float. Test a firm foot support before changing the desk legs.
Wrong hiking boots arrived: ordered size 40, box contains 43. Keep the label photo and ask the shop for a prepaid return.
Remote-day break idea: stand and refill water after each meeting. Calendar reminders alone get dismissed when I am editing.
Chair adjustment clip: backrest supports me only when reclined too far. Move it forward one notch and try the firm block under both feet.
Monitor riser correction: 12 cm is too tall with this screen. Lower to 7 cm; I was lifting my chin to read the top line.
Boot shop sent prepaid label. Return parcel needs the order slip inside; use the original box with the wrong size photographed first.
Seven, black support, Tuesday
Break log: back-to-back calls meant no water trip until lunch. Put a five-minute buffer after the recurring project meeting.
At 7 cm monitor lift the text is comfortable, but the webcam now looks over my head. Move the camera to the lower screen edge and test a call preview.
Chair trial notes: the firm foot block stopped me sliding forward. Mark the seat-height lever position so it is easy to restore after guests use it.
Courier scanned the boots return. Tracking shows first depot received; keep the receipt until the correct size or refund arrives.
Two short breaks happened today because I left the water bottle in the kitchen. The afternoon reminder still clashed with a call; move it later.
Call preview with camera below monitor makes the angle awkward. Try a small clamp beside the screen at eye level, without changing the readable screen height.
Foot support slips on the floor during typing. Add a nonslip pad and test whether the chair still rolls back freely when I stand.
Return resolved: shop refunded the hiking boots instead of replacing them. Match the amount to the card entry and close the parcel case.

The next desk check must adjust seat and screen together: lock in the chair height with feet supported, then reset the monitor riser so I can read without lifting my chin. Photograph both settings from the side for the home-work setup note.
Do that after the call, if it still feels wrong.
Work-break review after a week: the meeting buffer worked four days out of five. Keep it and add a brief walk after the final call, before evening chores.
Home desk side photo saved: feet on stable block, chair lever marked. Nonslip pad holds while allowing the chair to move when getting up.

b08.text: Afternoon workroom glare: window reflection sits over the spreadsheet totals. Start by rotating the desk a quarter turn, keeping the window to the side.
Shared desk handover annoys us both: Rui moves the chair and I lose the keyboard position. Make two simple setup cards with photos of our preferred arrangements.
Keyboard tray leaves the mouse too far right. Try the compact keyboard on the desktop and place the mouse close beside it.
Video-call preview: my face is dark against the bright window. Test the small diffused lamp beside the webcam rather than increasing screen brightness.
Quarter-turn desk trial leaves the reflection unchanged because the side cabinet mirror catches the window. Cover that mirror temporarily and retest the glare before moving furniture again.

Make the compact-keyboard and close-mouse positions comfortable first, then photograph them for my shared-desk reset card. I tried moving the mouse inward while keeping the wide keyboard, but my hand kept hitting the number pad. The smaller keyboard gives that space back without changing the desk itself. Check the cable slack at the new position; yesterday it pulled the mouse toward the back corner halfway through editing. Rui needs a separate picture showing the larger keyboard, because the number pad is useful for their work. We should each do a reset from the other person's arrangement, using only the pictures, and note anything that requires guessing. Put the unused keyboard in the side cubby with its connector visible. The handover should preserve both workable arrangements even when we swap during a short lunch break.
Call-light test with diffuser: even face exposure, but a bright circle reflects in glasses. Shift the lamp higher and farther left.
Covered mirror test at 15:00 cleared the reflection from spreadsheet totals. Fit a removable fabric panel over the mirror during afternoon work.
Document holder on the left forces repeated head turns while typing. Put it between keyboard and screen, with the page top low enough not to hide the display.
Piano tuning enquiry: upright near the workroom door has two wavering notes around middle C. Ask the tuner to check the sticking soft pedal too.
Reset cards printed: Rui's has the wide keyboard, mine the compact one. Store the unused keyboard upright in the side cubby and leave the cable accessible.
Higher call lamp removes the glasses reflection. Mark its swivel position so camera lighting can be restored before meetings.
Near the door / left one / too high
Tuner booked Wednesday morning. Move the workroom chair away from the upright so the front panel and pedal assembly are accessible.
Fabric mirror panel blocks glare but its loose edge brushes the screen. Clip the bottom corners so it stays flat during afternoon work.
Input-layout check after a long editing session: close mouse is easier to reach, document holder stays readable. Keep the compact keyboard and remove the unused tray from the setup plan.
Rui reset the shared desk from the photo in under two minutes. Add where the document holder is stored; that was the only missing instruction.
Upright tuning completed; wavering middle notes now stable. Soft pedal linkage adjusted and tested quietly with the tuner before paying.
Call lighting at dusk needs a lower lamp setting than midday. Save two labelled brightness positions beside the swivel mark.
Shared workroom handover cards updated with holder storage and cable path. Both users tried the revised instructions successfully this evening.

b09.text: Ferry interview with Mr Renn: ask how the last boat was signalled in fog, then let him describe an ordinary shift. Avoid starting with the closure dispute.
Shed roof panel has a split around the nail by the apple tree. Measure the overlap before ordering a replacement sheet.
Ferry voices permission sheet: distinguish archive storage, named quotation and public audio playback. Give speakers a copy with their chosen boxes marked.
Listening exhibit idea: visitors hear a bell, a short worker memory, then the river now. Keep the whole sequence under four minutes.
Renn recording, opening: 'You counted the bikes before the people. Once the deck got busy you couldn't see the wheels.' Note a follow-up about the ramp queue.

At the end of Renn's ferry interview, record his answer about the winter signal lamp, then read back the permission choices. He allows named archive access but has not agreed to public playback; put that limit on his signed sheet and the recording log.
Don't use the bit about his brother yet.
Shed replacement sheet cut to size. The old battens are solid; replace only the two rusty fixings and add washers under the new heads.
Exhibit prototype: fade the bell before the spoken voice begins. Visitors at the test table could not catch the first sentence over it.
Permission register entry for Elsie Dane: archive access and named quotations allowed; public sound playback allowed only for the two marked excerpts. Store her marked transcript with the form.
Dane transcript check: at 12:08 she says 'chain locker', not 'train locker'. Listen to the original once more before replacing the automatic transcript phrase.
Renn dates the new ferry shelter to 1964, the winter his eldest started work. Add that as his recollection, not an independently verified opening date.
Listening exhibit script uses Dane's marked queue excerpt and the river ambience. Total 3:42. Put a transcript at seated height beside the headphones.
Shed roof hose test: no drip at the new panel overlap. The door still sticks, but that is an older issue; the roof patch is sound.
Renn returned his permission form with archive-only choices unchanged. Log the received date and keep his audio out of the public-playback approved list.
The lamp was green, I think. Ask again.
Exhibit headphone lead snags on the table corner. Route it through a smooth guide and check a seated visitor can reach the volume control.
Renn phoned to correct the shelter date: it was 1962, not 1964; he had mixed it up with his son's later job. Append his correction to the interview transcript without deleting the original statement.
Dane approved the exhibit's exact edited queue excerpt after hearing it. Add this approval to her permission record; it does not extend to the rest of the interview.
Ferry listening station final check: transcript matches the audible edit, bell is quieter, and the player restarts after the final river sound.

b10.text: Market Street interview notebook: Bea remembers the shoe repair shop at number 14. Ask where deliveries entered and who shared the yard.
Tabletop radio tuning knob slips on its shaft. The grub screw turns but never tightens; inspect the brass insert before replacing the whole knob.
Walking booklet route begins at the old market arch, loops through Market Street, and ends at the pump. Aim for an easy 35-minute walk with six stops.
Museum owns the Market Street plan scan. Ask whether a 300-copy booklet run is allowed and what exact credit line they require.
Town archive deposit checklist for shopkeeper recordings: WAV files, transcripts, speaker release forms and a contents list. Keep restricted interviews in a clearly marked folder.
Bea corrects her earlier address: the shoe repair shop was 41 Market Street, not 14. Her father's invoice has the address; photograph it with her permission as supporting evidence.
Walking booklet stop 3: describe the shared yard before the shopfront. A visitor standing at the arch can still see the passage Bea described.
They said yes to the small one only.
Museum permits the plan in the 300 printed booklets, with 'Town Collection, plan drawer 8' beneath it. This permission does not include posting the full scan online.
Radio knob insert is stripped. A replacement insert grips properly; align the pointer at the dial's low end before tightening.

Shopkeeper transcript review: Bea says the yard smelled of leather glue, while Omar remembers roasting coffee next door. Keep both accounts with their speakers instead of merging them into one recollection.
Archive intake found two recordings without speaker release forms. Hold those files out of the deposit until the signed forms arrive; the other four packages can proceed.

Booklet map page: insert the museum's required credit exactly under the Market Street plan and note the 300-copy permission in the rights log. The PDF for public download should omit this plan because online reproduction was not granted.
Rename my 'Old shops chats' folder to 'Market Street testimony'. The invoices and interview transcripts should stay grouped by speaker inside it.
Maybe drawer eight? Can't read the last word.
Radio tracks stations smoothly across the dial now. Refit the back panel and keep the stripped insert to compare if it loosens again.

Before depositing Bea's interview, append her correction from 14 to 41 to the transcript and catalogue summary. Keep the original spoken address in the recording and include the invoice photo as a supporting research attachment in her archive package.
Walked the booklet route in 38 minutes. The pump stop has no safe standing space for a group; put the final paragraph at the bench before the corner instead.
Museum confirmed the credit proof is acceptable. Save that email with the signed plan reproduction permission, not just the printer's messages.
Town archive receipt lists four complete shopkeeper packages and two withheld. Their catalogue numbers match the contents list; retain the receipt alongside the release forms.

b11.text: Ridge race block, week one: easy runs Tuesday and Thursday, longer trail outing Sunday. Keep the first week familiar while I learn the park loop.
Bedroom dresser sale photos: include the scratched top and the drawer interiors. Listing dimensions are 110 wide, 45 deep, 82 high.
Ridge weekend booking: small guesthouse near the start has a twin room. Check whether Saturday arrival after 21:00 is possible before paying.
Shoe comparison log: blue pair grips the gravel turn better; grey pair feels less bulky on flat pavement. Repeat the same park circuit in each before choosing for Ridge.
Ridge week two long run planned for Sunday morning, two laps of the woodland loop. Carry the small map because I missed the north fork last time.
Guesthouse permits late check-in if we call before reception closes. The train arrives 20:40, with a short walk from the station.
Buyer's dresser question: all drawers slide, but the bottom one needs lifting slightly. Send a short video so that is clear before collection.

Catching up the Ridge diary for the opening woodland outing. I followed the north fork correctly this time and found that the climb comes much earlier in the lap than I remembered. The first lap felt rushed because I tried to stay with another runner all the way to the gate. On the second I let them go and finished feeling much more settled. For the next long outing, start on my own and use the gate as a reminder to check effort, not as a target time. The watch paused under the trees, so its average pace is not a useful comparison with my previous run. Keep the route and how the two laps felt in the log. I also liked having a few quiet minutes at the end before heading home.
Move week two's long trail run from Sunday to Saturday: family plans now fill Sunday morning. Keep the same two woodland laps; change only the day in the Ridge schedule.
Grey shoes on the park comparison circuit: heel slips on the uphill bend even with the laces adjusted. Blue pair stayed put on the earlier test.
The blue one, probably. Bring it Saturday.
Dresser buyer can collect Thursday at six. Measure the stair turn with the drawers removed before agreeing to carry it down together.
Ridge week four log: completed the midweek easy runs and one hilly outing. The new loop is more exposed than the woodland route; note that when comparing the two sessions.

Ridge race-week handoff: move the final short shakeout to Friday morning because Saturday is now the travel day. Reserve the earlier train and tell the guesthouse we expect to arrive at 18:00; update both the training calendar and trip booking note.
Shoe decision saved: blue pair for Ridge. Its heel stays secure and the gravel turns felt predictable on both comparison outings; pack spare laces with it.
Train change confirmed for the race weekend, arrival 17:35. Guesthouse acknowledged the 18:00 estimate and sent directions from the station.
Dresser collected, buyer checked the scratch and drawer before paying. Remove the listing and keep the collection message until the payment clears.
Ridge block last entry before travel: Friday shakeout done on the flat loop. Six weeks of notes saved together; don't compare the tree-covered GPS sections as if they were measured course splits.
Race guesthouse check-in smooth. Return-train tickets downloaded because the station signal was patchy on arrival.
Ridge finish reflection: starting calmly on the first climb helped. For the next training block, keep those woodland laps but practise the long descent earlier in the cycle.

b12.text: Four-week evening base block: aim for three regular outings each week. First priority is leaving work on time, so put the running kit beside the door in the morning.
Night relay team draft: Jo opens, I take second, Wen third, Sol anchors. Each leg uses the same riverside loop.
Balcony railing paint flakes where the flower boxes hang. Scrape a test patch and check if the old surface needs primer before buying the finish coat.
Headlamp bench check: broad beam lights the path edges; spot mode makes the central patch bright but hides roots beside it. Test both on the riverside bend.
Club route guide needs a clear start point for the riverside loop, gate opening times, and the muddy bypass. Draw it for someone who has never joined us before.
Evening block week one: two outings done, third moved to the weekend after a late work call. The flat circuit made it easy to get out without planning a route.
Relay roster change: Wen has a late shift, so swap his third leg with my second. New order Jo, Wen, me, Sol; tell the marshal before the entry deadline.
Route-guide photo at the riverside fork: the wooden post is obscured by leaves. Annotate the turn using the low brick wall as the landmark.

For tomorrow's base-block outing, run the riverside loop after dusk and test the broad-beam lamp on the rooty bend. Log the session as the week's third outing, and separately note whether the light stays steady when turning my head.
Primer trial on balcony railing dried smooth. Finish colour will be dark green; mask the pale wall before brushing near the brackets.
Wen has the spare. Ask before Friday.
Headlamp field result: broad beam showed the roots clearly but the strap slipped with every downhill step. Shorten the top strap and repeat a brief test before choosing it.
Night relay entry accepted with the revised order. Everyone needs their number collected by 19:00; I will bring the team envelope to the clock tower.
Base block midpoint: six evening outings across two weeks. Work ran late twice, so the weekend backup slot is worth keeping. No need to add missed minutes to the next run.
The last bit is dark. Mark it somehow.

Club guide field check: add an unlit-section symbol at the rooty riverside bend. My lamp test showed the broad beam is clearer there; finish the lamp comparison note with that finding and add a reminder to carry a light in the evening guide.
Balcony rail finish coat complete. Removed the masking while the edge was still soft; a small drip under the corner bracket needs touching up tomorrow.
Relay debrief: all four ran, but the second exchange was confusing near the spectators. Save the marshal's marked meeting point for our next team entry.
Evening block complete: eleven outings in four weeks. The riverside route stayed enjoyable, but the short flat circuit was what kept the workday habit practical.
